title: Region-level links from cell types, input wiring and Kv3 expression to spiking almost disappear inside 226 mouse brain regions (61,101 IBL units, Allen MERFISH and Knox voxel maps)
abstract: Question: earlier region-level studies found that the cell-type mix of a mouse brain region predicts its intrinsic spiking, that input wiring predicts task coding, and that Kv3 and Pvalb expression predict short spikes. Do these links also hold inside regions, at the 100-300 um scale? Data: 61,101 good IBL Brain-Wide Map units (689 probes, 139 mice, 226 regions) placed in the Allen CCF; local MERFISH neuron subclass mix (315 subclasses), local ipsilateral input density from the Knox 2019 voxel model (291 sources) and local gene expression, all smoothed with a 150 um kernel. We removed the mean of each probe-region group. A plan was frozen before the unit-level outcomes. Results (95% mouse bootstrap intervals): 61-81% of feature variance is inside groups, but units from different mice less than 100 um apart correlated at only 0.0062 (-0.0012 to 0.0150), so at most about 0.6% of it is a reproducible spatial map. Ridge mappings fitted on region means (cross-validated r 0.49 for cell types, 0.70 for input) gave within-group correlations of 0.029 (0.012 to 0.035) for cell types and 0.023 (0.012 to 0.031) for input. The cell-type transfer fell by 0.0097 (0.0037 to 0.0156) when units were moved 400-600 um along the probe; the input transfer did not pass this test. Mappings learned inside groups gave R2 below 0.0004 for held-out regions and up to 0.0013 for held-out mice, mostly shared by the two maps. Kv3 and Pvalb had Spearman rho -0.46 and -0.64 with spike duration across 191 regions, but within-group correlations of 0.003 (-0.010 to 0.018) and 0.002 (-0.021 to 0.023), against -0.062 and -0.103 expected from the between-region slopes, although the local Kv3 map replicated in a second MERFISH brain (r 0.80). Conclusion: the region-level links describe differences between regions, not gradients inside them. Limitations: about 100 um localization error, one smoothed voxel connectome, recorded units are a biased sample of neurons, associations only, and no unit-level task coding.

display.caption: (a) Ridge mappings from position, cell-type mix and input wiring predict region means (pale bars, 10-fold cross-validated r over 173 regions) but give within-group correlations of 0.016-0.029 when applied to single units inside probe-region groups (solid bars, 95% mouse bootstrap). (b) Per-feature within-group transfer for cell types and input, with the square root of the cross-mouse pair correlation (<100 um) as a ceiling. (c) Correlation of group-demeaned features for units of different mice against their distance.

(a, b) Spike duration against local Kv3 (mean log2 Kcnc1-3) and Pvalb: region means (gray) follow the between-region slope (dashed), but within-group deviations (blue, 20 bins) are flat. (c) Within-group slope divided by between-region slope, 95% mouse bootstrap. (d) Within-group correlation with spike duration for Kv3 and Pvalb against 1,000 random gene triplets, and the value expected from the between-region slope.

Misregistration curves: every unit of a probe is moved along the probe track and the local maps are resampled. (a) Within-group correlation of the between-region mappings; the cell-type curve falls away from the true position (planned peak test passed). (b) Out-of-region within-group R2 of mappings learned inside groups (x 1000); all values are near 0 at every shift.

citations.reason: We reuse its unit feature definitions and its IBL session-subject table, and we test its region-level cell-type and wiring links inside regions.
Its region-pair result (cell-type mix predicts intrinsic spiking) is the claim that we test at the within-region scale; the link is weak inside regions.
It found that Kv3 transcripts predict shorter spikes across regions; inside probe-region groups we found no Kv3 link.
It found that Kv3 expression predicts shorter spikes across 182 regions; we reuse its cluster-mean expression method and show that the link does not hold inside regions.
It reported a Kv3.1 link with spike duration brain-wide; the link is absent inside regions.
